title: Primrose Distribution inference integration notes
body:
Meeting date: 2025-09-26
Attendees: Diego Alvarez (Primrose), Sofia Martín (Primrose infra), Maya Patel (RW solutions), Liam Chen (RW serving), Rashmi Kapoor (RW security)

Purpose: capture customer constraints and quick technical plan for Primrose Distribution pilot — goal is in-warehouse inference for package routing assistant + OCR label normalization. Keep as field notes; will convert to PRD after validation.

Summary notes / raw capture:
- Primrose runs 6 warehouses; pilot target = 1 warehouse (Chicago) with 6 edge boxes. They want model to assist human packers: parse handwritten notes, recommend next-bin, and normalize address fragments into canonical form.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) — strong ask. Throughput: ~180 req/s steady (peak bursts to 400/s during shift change).
- Data sensitivity: label images contain PII (names, partial SSN-like ids). Cannot ship raw images off-prem. Need encryption at rest + limited telemetry; KMS integration required.
- Connectivity: warehouse has flaky internet (satellite backup). Solution must handle offline mode with local fallback. Primrose prefers VPC peering + private deploy; hosted API allowed as fallback only during outages.
- Model preference: they asked about Llama2-70B vs 13B. We recommended smaller quantized variants for edge. Proposal: RW-quant-13B-int8 + OCR postproc microservice. Need benchmark on A100 and on NVidia T4/T4e-equivalents (they plan to use RTX A30 on edge boxes).

Technical gotchas / unknowns to verify:
- GPU sizes on their edge boxes TBD (Sofia to confirm exact SKUs + memory per box). If memory < 40GB, 13B quant is necessary.
- Cold start tokenization overhead observed in prior pilots — need continuous warmup or a persistent warm worker per box. Check cost/ops impact.
- OCR latency: their current Tesseract pipeline is ~120ms per image. Combined with generation this might exceed SLO; consider batching or running OCR on separate cores.
- KV cache persistence across reboots: they want short-term session stickiness for repeated users (batching multiple label corrections). Evaluate disk-backed cache and restore time.
- Privacy masking: we need a redaction step before any telemetry leaves box. Confirm whether redaction can be entirely deterministic (regex for SSN/phones) or requires ML-based redactor.

Prompt / eval notes (quick sketch):
- Use a small set of 12 canonical prompts for initial OQ: address-normalize, extract-tracking-id, classify-damage, suggest-bin, correct-handwriting. Build eval set with 500 samples (images + expected canonical outputs).
- Quality target: address-normalize F1 >= 0.92 on canonical dataset. If quantization drops quality by >3 points, fallback to 1) different quant profile, or 2) push to larger model under lower-throughput route.

Operational plan (pilot-phase):
1) Sofia to confirm hardware specs by 2025-10-06.
2) RW to run local perf benchmarks: A) RTX A30 baseline (single box), B) 4x worker baseline on simulated edge (estimate throughput). Target deliverable: perf numbers + token cost estimate by 2025-10-10. (Owner: Liam)
3) Security review: Rashmi to draft minimal KMS/key rotation notes + telemetry redaction plan; Primrose legal to sign NDA addendum for PII handling. Target 2025-10-14.
4) Demo plan: deploy 1 box in staging with live OCR feed from Primrose (sanitized) — show 95th-latency and sample correction accuracy. Demo window target: 2025-10-20. (Owner: Maya)

Fallback policies & routing:
- Primary: private RW agent on edge (local model).
- Secondary: if local offline but network available and model degraded, route to Dedicated-instance (same region) with rate limit to protect cost.
- Tertiary: if Dedicated overloaded or unavailable, fall back (with redaction) to hosted API (must be explicit opt-in; Primrose currently disallows PII leaving, so hosted fallback requires further sign-off).

Open questions for Primrose (to get answers and reduce risk):
- Acceptable telemetry envelope: can we send token-level timing + anonymized counts only? Or nothing?
- Which encryption key provider? (Primrose KMS or RW-managed?)
- How often are label formats changed (seasonal SKUs)? Will need retrain/finetune cadence.

Quick risks (high-level):
- Latency multiplication (OCR + model + postproc) might push beyond SLO. Mitigation: move OCR to dedicated high-priority thread and tune batch sizes.
- Quantization quality regressions for handwriting normalization. Mitigation: run eval on 500-sample real-world handwriting set.
- Network outage -> degraded worker fallback complexity. Need robust state reconciliation for caching and audit logs.

Immediate next steps (short list):
- Maya: send perf-run checklist + model variants list to Primrose by 2025-09-29.
- Liam: schedule bench run on A30 + simulate T4 memory constraints (due 2025-10-10).
- Rashmi: draft redaction + KMS note and share with Primrose legal (due 2025-10-14).
- Diego/Sofia: confirm exact hardware + sample sanitized dataset (500 images) by 2025-10-06.

Notes to self: keep the pilot narrow: focus on address normalization first (highest ROI), defer free-form note generation until baseline quality is stable. Avoid recommending model >13B for edge unless Primrose upgrades hardware. Document all evaluation prompts and seed examples in repo PR after bench runs.

End of notes.
